questions.note: Hallux longest and 3-5 descend, but toe 2 ends about 12 mm short of the hallux (D19) and the 5th stands upright and apart, not rotated or curled under (D18). Toes have knuckles, but 2-4 are near-identical cylinders on pinched necks, splayed with even gaps (D1), ring-banded with lollipop pulps from below (D2) and crimped at the tips from the side (D10).

Both malleoli exist and the medial reads higher in V8, but the lateral is a broad blurred mound with no pointed tip (D13). The Achilles reads as a cord from behind with a lateral hollow; the medial hollow is weak and in profile there is no waist above the heel (D14). The heel joins the ankle with a ledge (D4). No anterior ankle crease in any view (D15).

defects.what: Toes 2-5 stand apart like fingers: an even dark gap between every toe, each toe joining the forefoot on a pinched neck behind a deep cleft, so the forefoot reads as a hand; real toes lie pressed together and are broadest at the web.
defects.fix: Close the gaps so neighbouring toes touch along their sides; make each toe widest at its base with shallow webs, tapering to the pulp, toes 3-5 converging slightly.

defects.what: From below, toes 2-5 are banded tubes: hard, evenly spaced ring creases around each phalanx and a small round pulp on a narrower stalk at each tip, like lollipops or ribbed hose.
defects.fix: The plantar toe is one soft pad per segment, the distal pulp the fullest and widest part; flexion creases are short shallow lines on the plantar side only, never rings.

defects.what: The heel from behind is a box: a flat broad posterior face, near-vertical straight sides and a flat bottom with squared corners, like a shoe last rather than a calcaneus wrapped in a fat pad.
defects.fix: A real heel from behind is a rounded inverted U: the tuberosity domes backward, the sides curve in above and swell slightly low where the pad spreads, the plantar edge fully rounded.

defects.what: On the lateral side the heel block starts with a ledge and a pinched notch below the lateral malleolus (also V1f near 1440,655-1477,718), so the heel reads as a separate piece stuck under the ankle.
defects.fix: Blend malleolus into calcaneus through one continuous soft hollow (the peroneal groove), with no step in the silhouette.

defects.what: The sole is a smooth slab with one long trough down its middle: no round heel pad, no lateral weight band, no medial arch hollow, no transverse ball pad or toe sulcus; it reads as a mannequin's sole.
defects.fix: Model the plantar landscape: round heel pad, narrow lateral band to the 5th head, concave medial arch, a full ball pad across the heads and a sulcus fold before the toes.

defects.what: The 1st metatarsal head is a small isolated knob jutting from the medial border (also in V1f and V5f), a bunion-like bump stuck on rather than the broad low bulge of the ball.
defects.fix: Spread the medial bulge over the head's ~14 mm radius and run it smoothly into the shaft and the hallux base.

defects.what: A small dark pit on the medial midfoot near the navicular: a dent with no anatomical cause where the navicular tuberosity should stand as a low dome.
defects.fix: A 12 mm dome about 2 mm proud with a soft hollow below and behind it into the arch.

defects.what: A thin straight vertical line below the medial malleolus, a mesh seam or crease artefact cutting otherwise smooth skin.
defects.fix: Remove it; the skin over the deltoid region is continuous.

defects.what: A small Y-shaped pinch crease on the lateral sole near mid-length, a mesh pinch rather than a skin fold.
defects.fix: Smooth it out; the lateral sole there is a flat, even weight-bearing band.

defects.what: Seen from the side the toes are a crumpled cluster: crimped tips with many small hard creases and a notched 5th-toe nub, reading as wrinkled plastic rather than fleshy toes.
defects.fix: From the side each toe shows a rounded pulp, a dorsal knuckle and a smooth curve down to the floor, with only a few soft creases at the joints.

defects.what: Jagged rippling folds at the base of toe 3 by the 2-3 cleft, a sawtooth patch where the toe joins the forefoot.
defects.fix: One or two soft dorsal skin folds at the MTP, smooth in between.

defects.what: A hard groove rings the hallux across its dorsum at the IP joint, so the big toe reads as two pieces joined at a seam.
defects.fix: The dorsal IP crease is a few short shallow wrinkles over the knuckle, fading out at the sides.

defects.what: The lateral malleolus is a broad, soft, blurred mound with no apex; the fibula's tip should be the sharper, more pointed of the two malleoli.
defects.fix: A narrower dome of about 24 mm with a defined tip and a crisp hollow behind and below it.

defects.what: In profile the back of the ankle runs straight down into a heel that bulges from about z 85, with no concave waist where the Achilles stands in front of the heel's back.
defects.fix: Pull the contour in above the tuberosity (insertion near z 52) so the tendon reads as a narrow cord and the heel projects behind it.

defects.what: No anterior ankle crease is visible at the front of the ankle in any view; the shin flows into the dorsum unbroken.
defects.fix: One shallow horizontal fold at the dorsiflexion line near z 80-84, bowed slightly toward the toes.

defects.what: The extensor tendons are a fan of thin, evenly spaced, sharp-edged strings laid on the dorsum, crisper than anything else on the foot, so the dorsum reads engraved rather than domed over tendons.
defects.fix: One broader EHL cord and four lower, softer EDL branches that rise out of and fade back into the dorsum.

defects.what: The 5th metatarsal styloid shows as an isolated pea-sized blob on the lateral border rather than a bony prominence flowing into the shaft.
defects.fix: Let the styloid rise from the 5th shaft as a tapered bony point, merging behind into the cuboid fullness.

defects.what: The 5th toe stands upright and apart from the 4th with its nail facing up, nearly as thick as the 4th; it is neither rotated nor curled under.
defects.fix: Rotate it 30-45 degrees onto its lateral side, curl it and tuck it against and partly under the 4th, nail facing outward.

defects.what: Toe 2 ends about 12 mm short of the hallux tip (read in the plan ortho and V4o), against 3-5 mm in the spec; the toe tips fall in a steep, even staircase.
defects.fix: Lengthen toe 2 so its tip sits 3-5 mm behind the hallux tip, toes 3-5 following in a curve.

ranked: [D1] The toes are splayed like fingers: even gaps between all five, each on a pinched neck behind a deep cleft. Real toes press together, broadest at the web; this alone makes the forefoot read as a 3D model.
[D3] The heel from behind is a box with a flat back, vertical sides and a flat squared bottom, a shoe last rather than a calcaneus in a rounded fat pad.
[D5] The sole is a blank slab with a central trough: no heel pad, lateral band, arch hollow, ball pad or toe sulcus. It is the mannequin view of the foot.
[D19] Toe 2 stops about 12 mm short of the hallux, not 3-5 mm, and the toe tips step down in a steep even staircase, which reads diagrammatic.
[D18] The 5th toe stands upright and separate with its nail up, as if a small copy of the 4th; a boot-wearing man's 5th toe is rotated onto its side and curled under the 4th.
[D2] From below, toes 2-5 are ribbed tubes with hard ring creases and small round pulps on stalks; real plantar toes are soft pads with the pulp the fullest part.
[D4] The heel looks stuck on: a ledge and notch where it meets the lateral malleolus (V8, also V1f), instead of one continuous form running through the peroneal hollow.
[D6] The 1st metatarsal head is a small knob jutting from the medial border, bunion-like, rather than the broad low bulge of the ball.
[D13] The lateral malleolus is a soft blurred mound with no apex; it should be the more pointed of the two, with a crisp hollow behind it.
[D14] The ankle profile has no Achilles waist: the back of the leg runs straight into the heel bulge, so the tendon never reads as a cord in side view.
[D10] The toes from the side are crimped and crumpled at the tips, with a notched 5th-toe nub, like wrinkled plastic.
[D7] A dark pit sits on the medial midfoot where the navicular tuberosity should be a low dome.
[D16] The extensor tendons are thin, evenly spaced, sharp-edged strings, the crispest relief on the foot, so the dorsum reads engraved instead of domed.
Detail is sharp on the dorsum and toes and absent everywhere else: the heel, ankle and sole are airbrushed and inflated, so the rearfoot reads younger and softer than a 40-year-old soldier's.
[D8] A thin vertical seam line runs below the medial malleolus in V2.
[D9] A Y-shaped pinch crease on the lateral sole in V4, a mesh artefact.
[D15] No anterior ankle crease in any view; the shin flows into the dorsum unbroken.
[D12] A hard groove rings the hallux at the IP joint, making the big toe look like two pieces joined.
[D11] A jagged sawtooth patch of ripples at the base of toe 3 by the 2-3 cleft (V5f).
[D17] The 5th metatarsal styloid is an isolated pea-sized blob rather than a bony point flowing into the shaft.
Declared but distorting: the out-of-scope veins are heavy enough to kink the dorsal profile in V2o and the medial border in V4o, which hides the true profile there; not scored.
